lesson.title: Two routes to high-risk classification
lesson.summary: Select the product route or listed-use route without treating classification as permission.

prerequisites.reason: The learner must identify what is being classified before learning the classification result.
Both routes depend on the function intended for the system.

blocks: **High-risk classification** brings a system into a defined regulatory category. Article 6 contains two routes. Paragraph 1 concerns certain products or safety components under listed product legislation; paragraph 2 concerns the use cases in Annex III.
The routes are additional to each other. A system can require analysis under both. A result under one route does not erase the other route or an Article 5 prohibition.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(1)–(4), Annexes I and III

blocks: For the **product route**, identify the product legislation in Annex I, whether the AI is itself a covered product or a safety component, and whether the relevant product must undergo third-party conformity assessment. The paragraph 1 conditions are cumulative.
Northbridge considers an AI-enabled protective device. Calling it safety-related is a starting fact, not sufficient proof of the entire product-route test.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(1)–(4), Annexes I and III

blocks: For the **listed-use route**, compare the intended purpose with each relevant Annex III point. These cover specified biometric, infrastructure, education, employment, services, enforcement, migration and justice/democratic uses.
Northbridge's applicant evaluation needs the employment points. 'It is office software' is too broad to decide this. Paragraph 3 then supplies a limited derogation and profiling rule, taught later.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(1)–(4), Annexes I and III

blocks: Keep three conclusions separate: whether a practice is prohibited, whether a system is high-risk, and which obligations apply when. Transparency and other law need separate checks too.

Write the exact route and facts supporting it. 'Low-risk because a human is present' is not an Article 6 test. The date rules are also separate: a later high-risk application date does not postpone all other duties.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(1)–(4), Annexes I and III

questions.prompt: A use is classified high-risk. What does this establish?

options.blocks: Its regulatory category, with other checks remaining
options.reason: Classification is not a blanket permission or completed compliance assessment.

options.blocks: That human review is never needed
options.reason: Classification does not remove applicable oversight duties.

options.reason: The listed-use route must still be examined.
